guide.title: Listening guide
guide.start: Choose Play to listen here. If a stream cannot play in your browser, use Listening page. Live radio uses internet data; FM and AM use a radio receiver.
guide.bitrate.title: kbps · Data rate
guide.bitrate: Kilobits per second. At 128 kbps, listening uses about 58 MB per hour, excluding connection overhead. Higher bitrate is not a quality score across different formats or broadcasts.
guide.codec.title: MP3, AAC and AAC+ · Audio formats
guide.codec: These formats compress audio for streaming. AAC+ is commonly called HE-AAC. Sound also depends on the original broadcast and encoding; a larger number does not always sound better.
guide.channels.title: Mono and stereo
guide.channels: Mono has one audio channel; stereo has two. Stereo can create a sense of space, but does not guarantee better sound.
guide.frequency.title: FM, AM, MHz and kHz
guide.frequency: FM and AM are ways to broadcast over the air. MHz and kHz are frequency units used to tune a physical radio. Frequencies depend on your location.
guide.playlist.title: M3U, HLS and stream URLs
guide.playlist: A stream URL points to live audio. M3U is a playlist of addresses, not a music download. HLS delivers audio in segments, often through an .m3u8 address; browser support varies.
guide.compatibility.title: When playback fails
guide.compatibility: Streams can move, go offline or be restricted. HTTP streams cannot play inside this HTTPS site. Use the listening page or copy the stream URL into a compatible player. Playback checks are snapshots, not guarantees.
